cohort: 20 patients with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) and 20 age and gender-matched healthy controls in Thailand
finding: While there was no significant difference in baseline fecal microbiota composition between IBS-D patients and controls, probiotic supplementation, although not significantly affecting symptom severity scales, led to improvements in bowel movements, urgency, and mucus in stool and increased the proportion of Bifidobacterium bifidum in the gut.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in baseline fecal microbiota between IBS-D patients and controls, and mode of birth was not a significant factor.
